title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Conflicts of Interest - Former Client
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is asked to represent an employer in a wrongful dismissal suit at the Human Rights Tribunal. The paralegal realizes they previously represented the complaining employee in an unrelated traffic ticket (POA) matter five years ago. Is the paralegal ethically permitted to accept the retainer from the employer?
options: No, a paralegal can never represent a party acting against a former client under any circumstances.

Yes, provided the new matter is entirely unrelated to the previous representation and the paralegal obtained no confidential information during the prior retainer that could be used against the former client.
Yes, but only if the paralegal receives permission from the Human Rights Tribunal.
No, the paralegal must wait at least seven years before acting against a former client.
questions.explain: Rule 3.04 regarding acting against a former client states that a paralegal shall not act against a former client in the same or a related matter, or when the paralegal has confidential information arising from the previous retainer that would prejudice the former client. If the matters are entirely unrelated (traffic ticket vs. human rights) and no relevant confidential info was obtained, it is permissible.
